primary.thesis: The mechanism is the UN General Assembly calendar. Netanyahu has used the UNGA general debate in Manhattan as a set-piece speech almost every year, including 2023, 2024 and 2025. The ICC warrant does not bind the United States, and federal protection as a visiting head of government keeps him safe from arrest regardless of NYC mayor Mamdani's rhetoric. With Israeli elections due by late October 2026, a UN podium speech and meetings in New York are valuable campaign theater. The 2026 high-level week falls in the last third of September, so the trip most likely happens between about Sept 22 and 30. There is no known reason for him to be in NYC in the last 8 days of August.

basket.reason: As of Aug 23, no UN session, White House visit or other event puts him in New York before Aug 31. Unscheduled trips to NYC are rare and would be announced well ahead for security reasons.
The UNGA general debate in late September is his habitual New York appearance. It is also a campaign-season stage and usually pairs with US meetings.
This is a superset of C2. If the September trip slips, the extra three months also leave room for a post-election visit or a UN Security Council appearance.

failure_narrative: Netanyahu skips UNGA and sends his UN ambassador or foreign minister, and no later NYC trip happens before year-end. This could come from a sharp security crisis at home: renewed war with Iran or Hezbollah, a major Gaza or West Bank escalation, or mass-casualty attacks that make leaving the country politically impossible. It could also come from coalition collapse or a campaign that makes a week abroad costly, or from a trial or legal development. A clash with Sukkot (about Sept 25 to Oct 2) or a security decision prompted by the city's arrest rhetoric could also lead him to travel only to Washington. If he loses the election and is not PM by year-end, even a C3 visit becomes unlikely. C1 would only fail through a surprise late-August NYC stop, which is improbable.
hedge_thesis: The worlds where Netanyahu does not leave Israel are mostly worlds with an acute regional military crisis, above all a new round of direct Israel-Iran or Israel-Hezbollah hostilities. Israeli prime ministers cancel or shorten foreign trips when they are running a war cabinet, as he did before. That same escalation hits the Persian Gulf energy complex. Threats to Iranian export capacity or to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea push Brent crude, tanker rates and gold up and lift defense contractors. So a long position on Gulf oil and safe-haven or defense exposure tends to pay off in exactly the worlds where the NYC-visit basket loses.
